explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The text says the son of the Israelite woman "blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:11) That's why they bring him to Moses, Israel's leader. I think everybody in that camp stopped what they were doing.

explanations.answer: He steals from the man's tent
explanations.explanation: No stealing in this passage, friend. The fight breaks out first, and then the son of the Israelite woman "blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:11) The text never mentions a tent being robbed. Don't go adding things to the dough that the recipe never called for.

explanations.answer: He runs off from the camp
explanations.explanation: He doesn't run anywhere. The text says he goes out among the Israelites, a fight breaks out in the camp, and then he "blasphemed the Name with a curse." (Leviticus 24:10-11) After that, they bring him to Moses, Israel's leader. So he's still right there in the camp.

Right on the money. The text says, "They placed him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) Nobody rushes a decision here. They hold him and wait for the LORD to speak.

explanations.answer: They send him back to his tent
explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. Nobody sends him home to think about it. The text says, "They placed him in custody…" (Leviticus 24:12) He's held while they wait.

explanations.answer: They hand him over to his family
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. It says they placed him in custody, and the only person named in his family is his mother, Shelomith. (Leviticus 24:11-12) Nobody hands him off to anybody. He's held until the will of the LORD is made clear.

Yes, friend. They hold him "until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) They don't guess and they don't vote. They wait on the LORD, and then the LORD speaks to Moses. (Leviticus 24:13)

Close, but no elders here. The text says they held him "until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) The decision isn't left to a panel. They wait to hear from the LORD.

No judges in this one, baker. The text says they held him "until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them." (Leviticus 24:12) The people wait for the LORD Himself, and then He speaks to Moses. (Leviticus 24:13)

That's right. The LORD says, "…have all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then have the whole assembly stone him." (Leviticus 24:14) The ones who heard it are the ones who lay on their hands. It's a heavy moment, so I'll leave it right there.
Not the priests alone, friend. The LORD says, "…have all who heard him lay their hands on his head…" (Leviticus 24:14) It's the people who heard him, not a set group of priests.

The text doesn't point to family. It says, "…have all who heard him lay their hands on his head…" (Leviticus 24:14) The ones who heard him are the ones who do it. His mother, Shelomith, is named earlier, but she isn't given this part.

Careful, baker, that one's a trap. The LORD says the whole assembly must stone him, "whether he is a foreign resident or native." (Leviticus 16:16 is wrong, so look at Leviticus 24:16.) The law covers both. Nobody gets left out of it.

Yes, friend, it's false. The LORD says, "…the whole assembly must surely stone him, whether he is a foreign resident or native…" (Leviticus 24:16) The law covers both the foreign resident and the native. Same standard for everybody.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "Whoever kills an animal must make restitution…" (Leviticus 24:18) and then, "…whoever kills a man must be put to death." (Leviticus 24:21) Those are two different cases with two different outcomes.

It's true, friend. The text says, "Whoever kills an animal must make restitution…" (Leviticus 24:18) Death is for the one who "kills a man." (Leviticus 24:21) So restitution is the answer for the animal.
You got it, baker. The LORD says, "Just as he injured the other person, the same must be inflicted on him." (Leviticus 24:20) It's the same injury, no more and no less. The law matches the harm.

No doubling here, friend. The LORD says, "…whatever he has done must be done to him." (Leviticus 24:19) The text says "fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth." (Leviticus 24:20) That's the same, not double.

The text doesn't leave it open. The LORD says, "…whatever he has done must be done to him." (Leviticus 24:19) It names it plainly: "fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth." (Leviticus 24:20)

explanations.answer: He is the LORD their God
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The LORD says, "You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 24:22) That's the reason He gives, and it's all He says.

explanations.answer: The tribes asked Him for it
explanations.explanation: The text never says the tribes asked. The reason given is, "…for I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 24:22) The LORD gives the law Himself.

explanations.answer: Moses could not judge each case
explanations.explanation: That's not in the text, friend. The reason the LORD gives is, "…for I am the LORD your God." (Leviticus 24:22) Nothing is said about Moses being overloaded. Moses is the one who passes the word along.
